questions.q:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. The movie, B. which you recommended, C. was both interesting D. and entertain.
questions.solution:
Both … and joins parallel forms. Interesting is an adjective, so entertain must be replaced by entertaining.

**Answer: and entertain.**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: **Abrogate**
questions.solution:
Abrogate means formally repeal or abolish a rule or agreement. Repeal is the closest synonym.

**Answer: Repeal**

questions.q: **Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb:** She was so overwhelmed with tasks that she had to ____ some responsibilities to her assistant.
questions.solution:
Hand over means transfer responsibility or control to another person. This fits delegating tasks to an assistant.

**Answer: hand over**

questions.q:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrase:**

Due to the budget cuts, the organization had to operate strictly _______.
questions.solution:
On a shoestring means with very little money. The budget cuts therefore require operating on a shoestring.

**Answer: on a shoestring**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: **EPISTEMIC**
questions.solution:
Epistemic means relating to knowledge or the basis of knowledge.

**Answer: Knowledge-related**

questions.q:
Which of the following sentences uses the word "close" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence?

"Please be sure to close the door when you leave"
options: She lives very close to the library.
The museum is close to the park.
It’s a good idea to close all the windows before it starts to rain.
He keeps his family photos close to his bed.
questions.solution:
Close the door means shut it. Closing windows uses the same verb meaning; the other options describe proximity or closeness.

**Answer: It’s a good idea to close all the windows before it starts to rain.**

questions.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **Sit on the fence**
options: To be very decisive about a matter
To refuse to give an opinion or take a side
To be in a neutral, relaxed position
questions.solution:
Sitting on the fence means avoiding a decision or refusing to take either side.

**Answer: To refuse to give an opinion or take a side**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Futile**
questions.solution:
Futile means ineffective or useless. Effective is the opposite.

**Answer: Effective**

questions.q:
**Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who studies the stars and space**
questions.solution:
An astronomer studies stars and space scientifically. Astrology concerns beliefs about celestial influences.

**Answer: Astronomer**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Garrulous**
questions.solution:
Garrulous means excessively talkative. Quiet is the opposite.

**Answer: Quiet**

questions.q: **Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.** The tour guide said, "We have been walking for hours, but the ruins we have been looking for are just around this corner, and we will be there in a few minutes."
options: The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.
The tour guide said that we have been walking for hours, but the ruins we have been looking for are just around this corner, and we will be there in a few minutes.
The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for are just around that corner, and they will be there in a few minutes.
The tour guide said that they were walking for hours, but the ruins they were looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.
questions.solution:
In reported speech, have been changes to had been, are changes to were, will to would, this to that, and we to they.

**Answer: The tour guide said that they had been walking for hours, but the ruins they had been looking for were just around that corner, and they would be there in a few minutes.**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence :

The manager was asked to write a report __**in a quick, detailed and in a thorough manner.**__
options: in a quick, detailed, and thorough manner
in a quick, detailed and in thorough manner
in a quick, detailing and thorough manner
questions.solution:
Keep all three adjectives parallel under one shared phrase: in a quick, detailed, and thorough manner.

**Answer: in a quick, detailed, and thorough manner**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The country has at least twenty colleges __**of whom only six are officially recognized.**__
options: of whom only six are officially recognized
of whom only six have been officially recognized
of which only six has official recognition
Of which only six are officially recognized
questions.solution:
Colleges are things, so use which rather than whom. Six is plural, so the verb is are.

**Answer: Of which only six are officially recognized**

questions.q:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

Will the company launch the new product?
options: The new product will be launched by the company?
Will the new product be launched by the company?
Is the new product launched by the company?
The new product would be launched by the company?
questions.solution:
Move the new product to subject position. A future passive question uses Will + subject + be launched.

**Answer: Will the new product be launched by the company?**

questions.q:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

He said to her that the film they had watched the previous night was not as good as he had expected it to be.
options: He said to her, "The film we watched last night was not as good as I expected it to be."
He said to her, "The film we had watched last night was not as good as I had expected it to be."
He said to her, "The film we watched the previous night was not as good as I expected it to be."
He said to her, "The film we had watched last night was not as good as I expected it to be."
questions.solution:
Return the reported pronouns and time expressions to direct form: we, I and last night. Had watched and had expected return to watched and expected.

**Answer: He said to her, "The film we watched last night was not as good as I expected it to be."**

questions.q:
**Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:**

P: The restoration project was hailed as a triumph of community and expert cooperation

Q: The valuable texts and historic architecture of the old library were preserved throughout its restoration.

R: The library quickly gained international recognition as a cultural icon.

S: To guarantee the restoration’s correctness, local historians and preservationists collaborated.
questions.solution:
Q introduces the restoration. S explains the collaboration, P describes its success, and R gives the resulting recognition.

**Answer: Q, S, P, R**
